d: Mid-century speculative masterpieces reshaping the Solar System by Alfred Bester and Kurt Vonnegut.

titan.x: Serene estate beside the liquid methane seas where Winston Niles Rumfoord materializes and the robotic messenger Salo waits with the message from Tralfamadore.

mercury.x: Deep subterranean caverns where the glowing, paper-thin Harmonium creatures live on melodic vibrations and solar energy.

mars.x: Brainwashed human army assembled under Winston Niles Rumfoord in The Sirens of Titan, and oligarchic jaunte-landing domains in The Stars My Destination.

callisto.x: Outer Jovian colony and commercial enclave connected by personal teleportation (jaunting) across the warring planetary factions.

ceres.x: Derelict merchant vessel Nomad drifting in the Asteroid Belt where Gulliver Foyle is marooned, igniting his obsessive quest for vengeance.

b.s: Pioneering satire, cyberpunk precursors, and existential odysseys across the planets, from Alfred Bester’s teleportation-driven Solar System in The Stars My Destination to Kurt Vonnegut’s philosophical journey to Titan in The Sirens of Titan.
b.r: The Stars My Destination (1956) & The Sirens of Titan (1959)
